meaning: The number 26,000 appears in the Bible in connection with military musters and can also be linked to God's name YHWH (gematria value 26) multiplied by 1,000, symbolizing God's infinite greatness and perfection.
description:
The number 26000 appears in the Bible in connection with military musters. In Judges 20:15, 26000 Benjaminites capable of drawing swords are mustered to fight against the other Israelite tribes, and in 1 Chronicles 7:40, 26000 fighting men are counted among Asher's descendants. In both cases, it concerns the military strength of the tribes at a time when the people's organization and combat power were decisive.

In Jewish tradition, the number can also be interpreted symbolically. God's holy name YHWH has a gematria value of 26, and when this is multiplied by 1000 – a number that in biblical context often expresses perfection and infinity – 26000 emerges as an image of God's boundless power and majesty. Although this connection is a derived interpretation rather than an explicit biblical teaching, it gives the number an interesting symbolic dimension.

versions.meaning: The number 26,000 may be connected to God's name YHWH (which has the numerical value 26 in gematria) multiplied by 1,000, thus symbolizing God's infinite greatness and perfection.
versions.description: In Jewish gematria, the four letters of God's name YHWH (יהוה) have the numerical value 26 (Yod=10, He=5, Vav=6, He=5). The number 1,000 often represents completeness, greatness, or infinity in a biblical context. Thus, 26,000 can be interpreted as an amplification of the holy name of God, pointing to God's boundless power and majesty. However, this is a derived interpretation, and the number 26,000 itself plays no prominent direct role in the biblical texts.

footnotes.text: In Jewish gematria, the four letters in YHWH (יהוה) have the following numerical values: Yod (י) = 10, He (ה) = 5, Vav (ו) = 6, He (ה) = 5, which together total 26.

The number 1,000 (Heb. 'elef', אלף) is often used in the Bible to express a very large or complete number, as in Psalm 50:10 ('the cattle on a thousand hills') and Deuteronomy 7:9 ('keeps covenant and steadfast love for a thousand generations').
The 26,000 warriors of the Benjaminites in Judges 20:15 were part of a civil war that nearly wiped out the entire tribe of Benjamin—one of the most dramatic internal conflicts in Israel's history.
